articles.description:
Hello friends,
In this third article of our Git in Depth series, we'll try to learn and understand the topic of "interactive rebase".
As you can tell from the title, interactive rebase is used to change/rewrite our git history.
However, we need to keep the following warning in mind. Never rebase shared commits. Changes made to the past, especially on remote repos, can be very exhausting.
But again, for example, if a piece of information that shouldn't have been shared was written to the history, it may need to be deleted. For this, the best method is actually to delete a specific file or text from the entire history with the BFG tool. For details, you can check out this link.
The git blame command gives all the changes made in a file and their commit information.
git blame DOSYA_ADI

Hello,
In this article, we'll examine the options of the git merge command, which we use when combining our commits, that are used to manage the change it makes to the git history during the merge.
No Fast-forward
Fast-forward
Fast-forward Only
We'll also try to understand the git _rebase and git cherry-pick commands, which change the history, by examining their relationship with and differences from the git merge command.
These topics are usually covered in resources under the title "merge strategies", but that's an incorrect definition. If you look at the official git documentation as well, you can see that the word strategies refers to the techniques used while resolving conflicts. It's also possible to use these techniques as options in merge operations.

articles.author: murat cabuk
articles.description:
Hello, in this article we'll try to examine how Git organizes and manages files.
Basically, Git performs four fundamental functions.
Distribution of Repositories (Distributed Structure)
Branching and Corrections
Versioning and Content Tracking
Storing objects as key-value pairs.

Let's start examining from the inside out.
Key Value Store
The hash (sha1) of every file is kept, and changes are tracked on top of it. Folders, and even commits, have a hash too.
For example, with the code below we get the hash of a string input.
echo "merhaba dünya" | git hash-object --stdin

# 2ad1d25f2216c4cf25cbfb508d485f2350f317d8

If we make even the slightest change to this string, the hash changes. This means the file has changed.
echo "merhaba dünya " | git hash-object --stdin
dd38a8c3d16d052a1b43ad96172…
articles.title: Git in Depth 1: How Git Works

articles.description:
You set up a paid campaign on Meta, Google Search, or LinkedIn. You dial in your audience targeting, write crisp ad creative, configure conversion tracking, and allocate €2,000 to €10,000 for the month. Your cost per click settles somewhere between €3.50 and €11.00. The dashboard reports hundreds of clicks flooding into your site.
Then you open your web analytics, and the reality hits like a brick wall: 68% to 84% of those paid visitors leave within five seconds. They do not scroll down. They do not read your feature grid. They do not click your pricing tab. They never see your customer testimonials or your carefully produced product demo video. They arrived, blinked, felt confused or uninspired, and tapped the back button.
Where did your ad spend go? It did not get lost in the footer or d…

Online shops, banks, transport companies, e-book sellers and a few other sectors in the EU now have a legal duty to make their websites usable for people with disabilities. I wanted to know how far the average company actually is from that, so I tested homepages.

I train people who write software, and people who decide which tools those teams will use. articles.author: Susumu Takahashi
articles.description:
When you edit a post in WordPress and click "Update", a "Revisions" item appears in the sidebar, letting you compare earlier versions and restore one. It is a useful safety net against accidental overwrites. At the same time, maintenance advice often warns that revisions pile up in the database and should be capped.
Where exactly are revisions stored, and in what form? How do they differ from autosaves and auto-drafts? As promised at the end of the previous article on autoload options, this post answers those questions using read-only queries against this blog's own WordPress database (7.1 series) and the core source code.
Revisions have no table of their own. They are stored in wp_posts, as rows whose post_type is revision. Grouping this blog's wp_posts by type and status (with SELECT onl…
articles.title: How WordPress Revisions, Autosaves and Auto-Drafts Work — and How to Manage the History in Your Database

Healthcare AI systems depend on accurate patient records. However, integrating information from multiple sources creates an important challenge: establishing that the records being analysed belong to the same individual.
A model can process data accurately and still produce an unsafe recommendation if patient identity is incorrect.
The patient matching problem
Healthcare environments may contain duplicate records, inconsistent identifiers, spelling variations, incomplete demographic information, and different patient identification systems across institutions.
Consider a patient receiving care from two hospitals. Each organisation maintains a separate identifier, and some demographic details differ.
An AI system attempting to integrate these records must determine whether they represent th…
articles.title: Patient Identity Resolution: A Fundamental Safety Requirement for Healthcare AI
